resolutions.researcher_notes: The pipeline's real name is Gamasa–Finosa/Fenosa (خط غاز جمصة – فينوسا); 'Veunsa' is a garbled transliteration of فينوسا. Egyptian Presidency national-projects page describes the line as built/added in 2015 to supply the West Damietta power plant; youm7 reports construction completed Nov 2015 and the plant being fed gas. Both establish operating status. Note: the original current_ref petro-news.com/95212 (flagged DEAD_LINK in the brief) is in fact live again (verified 200, mentions the جمصة-فينوسا line among Egypt's implemented gas projects) and could stay as a supporting cite.
StartYear1=2015 corroborated by two independent sources: Presidency page says the Gamasa–Finosa line was 'added during 2015'; youm7 reports construction completed November 2015. Consistent.

VALUE CONTRADICTION — UNIT MISMATCH. youm7 (and the pipeline's popular name) give the design flow as 6.8 million CUBIC METRES per day (6.8 مليون متر مكعب يوميا), i.e. ~6.8 MMcm/d ≈ 240 MMcf/d. GEM records Capacity=6.80 in MMcf/d, which mistakes cubic metres for cubic feet and understates the flow by ~35x. The '6.8' figure is supported by a single strong source; recommend Update either correct CapacityUnits to MMcm/d or convert to ~240 MMcf/d. No independent second source states a capacity figure.

Both sources place the line in Damietta governorate, Egypt: it runs from chamber No.10 on the Idku–Damietta 32-inch line at Gamasa (جمصة, Damietta gov.) to the Finosa/West Damietta power-plant intake. Supports StartState/Province=Damietta, Start/End CountryOrArea=Egypt (34 km, 42-inch per both sources).

VALUE CONTRADICTION. Three independent sources (Presidency, youm7, petro-news) all state the cost as ~397 million EGP (~US$50.4M); youm7 gives 'approximately 397 million pounds'. GEM records SegmentCost=340,000,000 EGP, which no source supports. Refs added but recommend Update revise SegmentCost to 397,000,000 EGP (or flag the delta).

Status 'operating' inferred from context: both sources report gas began flowing through the line (reversed direction, Israel→Egypt) in January 2020 and it is actively carrying gas — Al Jazeera 'Egypt started importing natural gas from Israel's Leviathan field on Wednesday'; World Oil 'Israeli gas finally reaches Egypt'. Two independent outlets. Line is currently operating.

Fuel=Gas: gulfoilandgas describes 'a submarine gas pipeline ... to transport approximately 7.0 BCM per annum of Egyptian natural gas'; INSS refers to it as a natural gas pipeline carrying 7-9 BCM. Two independent sources, both explicit natural gas.

StartYear1=2008 supported by gulfoilandgas milestones: 'Completion 2/25/2008' / 'The commissioning of the pipeline began' 2/25/2008 (original Egypt→Israel operation). StartYear2=2020 supported by Al Jazeera: Egypt began importing Israeli gas in January 2020 after the flow was reversed. Both start years independently sourced.

StopYear=2012: LA Times (23 Apr 2012) reports the Egypt-Israel gas deal was revoked in April 2012; Washington Institute states the flow 'was halted in 2012 following the election of a Muslim Brotherhood-led government and multiple terrorist attacks on the pipeline'. Two independent sources confirm the 2012 shutdown of the original Egypt→Israel flow.

Capacity=7.00 bcm/y: gulfoilandgas 'transport approximately 7.0 BCM per annum'; INSS notes upgrades 'have the potential capacity to increase the annual flow capacity, from 7 to 9 BCM' (i.e. baseline 7 BCM). Two independent sources agree on 7 bcm/y.

LengthKnown=90 km: INSS 'the 90 km pipeline from el-Arish to Ashkelon'; Offshore Technology 'the 90km EMG pipeline connects the Israeli and Egyptian pipeline networks'. Two independent sources agree on 90 km. CONTRADICTION FLAG: gulfoilandgas states '100 kilometres (62 mile)' for the same line — minority figure; the 90 km value has stronger corroboration and matches the GEM value.

FuelSource=Egypt supported for the ORIGINAL (2008-2012) design only: gulfoilandgas 'transport ... Egyptian natural gas to Israel'; Washington Institute 'originally built to supply Egyptian gas to Israel'. CONTRADICTION FLAG for review: since the 2020 reversal the physical fuel source is now ISRAEL (Tamar/Leviathan offshore fields → Egypt), per Al Jazeera and the OPIC/DFC project description (rightsindevelopment). The FuelSource=Egypt field reflects the pipeline's original configuration, not its current direction — flag for Update to decide whether it should reflect current (Israel) source.

Endpoints Ashkelon (Israel) ↔ El-Arish/Arish, North Sinai (Egypt): INSS 'the 90 km pipeline from el-Arish to Ashkelon'; OPIC/DFC project page (rightsindevelopment) 'a pipeline running from Al-Arish, Egypt, to Ashkelon, Israel'. Washington Institute separately places al-Arish in North Sinai. Two+ independent sources confirm both endpoints and countries.

Status 'operating' confirmed by two independent sources. EGAS (official Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co) history timeline: 'Start of Arab Gas Pipeline operations — Egypt's first natural gas export pipeline project' (2003) and 'Resumption of gas exports to Jordan via the Arab Gas Pipeline after a four-year halt' (2019). Attaqa (Nov 2024) describes the line still carrying gas: Egypt-Jordan flow resumed 2018 after Zohr, and Israeli gas flowing through it to Jordan since 2020, with Arish as the junction point. Syrian Observer (2021, verified live) 'Arab Gas Pipeline Ready, Syria Gets Egyptian Gas' further corroborates. The two current refs (kingabdullah.jo inauguration + attaqa) were flagged DEAD_LINK in the brief but both re-verify live (200); the Egyptian Arish-Taba segment is the operating export feeder.

VALUE CONTRADICTION FLAGGED. The current ref hydrocarbons-technology.com now 301-redirects to offshore-technology.com/projects/arab-gas-pipeline-agp/ (same content, live). That page states: 'The first phase (Arish-Aqaba section), commissioned in July 2003 at an investment of $220m' — corroborating the year (2003) and USD unit, but giving $220,000,000, NOT the GEM value $207,550,000. The $220m consistently appears across mirrors (Wikipedia, oilgasstoragenews, oilandgasadvancement) but all trace to the same offshore-technology profile, so this is effectively a single independent origin (independent=false). No source anywhere states $207.55m exactly. Possible reconciliation: $220m is the full Arish-Aqaba first phase (250km overland Arish-Taba + 15km subsea Taba-Aqaba + compressor/metering stations); GEM's $207.55m may be an overland-Arish-Taba-only subset, but this is unverified. Recommend Update review the SegmentCost figure against the source's $220m.

Both brief-current URLs (attaqa.net, kingabdullah.jo) now actually resolve 200 OK (re-checked with url_verifier), contra the brief's DEAD_LINK flag, but neither confirms current ('operating') status: kingabdullah.jo is the 2003 inauguration announcement (historical only, contains 'طابا'/Taba); attaqa.net (Nov 2024) discusses possible future re-routing, not current flow, and does not mention Taba specifically. Replaced with two independent 2024-2025 trade-press sources describing the Taba-Aqaba (Egypt-Jordan) link as an active, in-use physical connection: World Pipelines (Dec 2024) reports Jordan-Egypt LNG/FSRU deal moving 'gas supplies...through the existing pipeline network linking the two countries'; Egypt Oil & Gas (2025, Energos Force FSRU arrival) reports the FSRU's 'connection to the Arab Gas Pipeline will enable Egypt to tap into LNG supplies' at Aqaba. Neither is a bare 'currently flowing today' snapshot, so tier=medium rather than high. IMPORTANT CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: Enab Baladi (Jan 2026, English) reports Jordan's Ministry of Energy explicitly denying that gas newly reaching Syria via Aqaba is Egyptian -- it is regasified LNG, not gas pumped through the Egypt-Taba-Aqaba subsea pipe. So the Taba-Aqaba segment's *direct* Egypt-to-Jordan gas flow appears intermittent/underutilized in 2025-2026 even though the physical link remains in commercial use (LNG-swap arrangement) -- worth a human check if GEM wants finer status granularity than 'operating' vs 'idle'. Searched: Arabic (attaqa.net, kingabdullah.jo) + English trade press (World Pipelines, Egypt Oil & Gas, OGJ, S&P Global, Enab Baladi) via WebSearch/WebFetch; no fabricated URLs; gem.wiki/GEM used only as a lead, not cited.

Status 'operating' inferred from two independent inauguration reports: Petroleum Africa (Mubarak inaugurated the completed Upper Egypt line late Dec 2010 / early Jan 2011, final Sohag-Aswan phase commissioned Nov 2010) and al-Masry al-Youm (خط غاز الصعيد inaugurated by Mubarak in Aswan, Thu 30 Dec 2010). Both describe a completed, gas-carrying line -> operating. NOTE: the brief's current_ref (almasryalyoum details/103848) was flagged DEAD_LINK but resolves 200 today (false-negative); retained.

StartYear1=2009 supported by al-Masry al-Youm: the sixth/final phase (Girga-Aswan) 'الانتهاء منها في نوفمبر 2009' (completed Nov 2009). One strong Arabic source. CONTRADICTION/NUANCE to flag: the OFFICIAL inauguration was 30 Dec 2010 (al-Masry) and Petroleum Africa dates commissioning/inauguration to late 2010-Jan 2011; so 2009 = physical completion of the last stage, 2010 = ceremonial start-up. StartYear1=2009 is defensible as physical completion but the sheet may want 2010 for operational start.

Capacity=12.00 bcm/y supported by Petroleum Africa: 'With a current capacity of 8 bcm annually, capacity is expected to reach 12 bcm by 2014.' Single source. NUANCE to flag: 12 bcm is the DESIGN/target capacity (by 2014); throughput at inauguration was 8 bcm/y. al-Masry al-Youm gives no capacity figure; no second independent corroboration found for 12 bcm.

LengthKnown=930 km corroborated by two independent sources: al-Masry al-Youm ('الطول الإجمالي 930 كيلومتر') and Petroleum Africa ('The 930 km pipeline'). Minor discrepancy to note: Petroleum Africa's inauguration article and OGJ (2007) cite ~794-800 km, which are earlier partial-network figures before the full Dahshour-Aswan extension; 930 km is the completed full-network length.

Diameter values 32 and 30 in corroborated: Petroleum Africa gives per-segment diameters (Minya-Assiut 32 in; Assiut-Sohag 30 in; Sohag-Aswan 408 km 30 in) and OGJ gives 32 in for the Beni Suef/Abu Qorqas and Menya-Assiut phases; al-Masry al-Youm states diameters of '30 و32 بوصة'. CONTRADICTION to flag: the sheet's leading 36-inch value ('36, 32, 32, 32, 32, 30') is NOT supported by any source found — every source caps the multi-segment diameters at 32 in. The 30/32 values are solid; the 36 is unverified.

Route Dahshour (Giza) -> Aswan corroborated by two independent sources: al-Masry al-Youm (start دهشور, end أسوان) and Petroleum Africa (Cairo/Dahshour through Beni Suef, Minya, Assiut, Sohag to Aswan). StartLocation=Dahshour and EndLocation=Aswan both directly supported.

SegmentCost=9,300,000,000 USD literally matches Petroleum Africa: 'The 930 km pipeline was worth approximately $9.3 billion in investments.' STRONG CONTRADICTION to flag: two independent sources give a far lower cost in Egyptian pounds - al-Masry al-Youm 'حوالى 5.7 مليار جنيه' (~5.7 bn EGP) and Petroleum Africa's own inauguration article 'LE5.7 billion'. 5.7 bn EGP at 2010 rates is ~USD 1 bn, an order of magnitude below 9.3 bn. $9.3 bn for a 930 km gas line (~$10 M/km) is implausibly high and likely a units error (EGP mis-stated as USD) in the single source that matches the sheet. Value is technically sourced but low-confidence; recommend reviewing toward ~5.7 bn EGP.

Value = operating. Both Argaam and Shorouk (independent Egyptian daily) report the petroleum sector completed (انتهاء/انتهى تنفيذ) the Nubaria–Sadat line, dated 2014-10-03; completed = operating. NOTE: brief marked the Argaam URL DEAD_LINK, but it now returns 200 and contains النوبارية (re-verified live), so it is retained and corroborated.

Value = 73 km. Argaam and Shorouk both state 'بطول 73 كم وقطر 36 بوصة' (73 km, 36-inch). CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: egy-map.com (Egypt's Projects Map, aggregator) reports 70 km — a minor rounding discrepancy from a weaker source; the two independent 73 km sources are preferred.

Sadat City is in Monufia governorate; supports endpoint locations.

Value = 495,000,000 EGP. Argaam states the Nubaria–Sadat line was executed 'باستثمارات 495 مليون جنيه' (495 million EGP). Shorouk's headline figure of 590 million EGP is the COMBINED total for BOTH the Nubaria–Sadat AND the Edfu lines ('خطي غاز النوبارية–السادات وإدفو بـ590 مليون جنيه'); the 495M sheet value for this segment alone is consistent. egy-map reports 700M (weaker aggregator, not preferred).

Original live current_ref (youm7.com) is dead; revived via Wayback (2020 capture, HTTP 200, content verified). Cross-checked against two independent World Bank documents for the same project (EG-Giza North Power Project, P116194): the 2016/2017 ESIA (documents1.worldbank.org/.../SFG1795-V7-EA-P116194...txt, verified OK) which describes 'El Mahmodia Power Station (27 km + 17 km + 7 km) + gas decompression station' -- length sums to 51 km, consistent with the 52 km figure (rounding/measurement basis differs slightly) -- and the 2018 Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review (documents1.worldbank.org/.../Egypt-Arab-Republic-of-EG-Giza-North-Power-Project.pdf) which confirms four of the six power-plant gas pipelines financed under this project were completed by the loan's closing date (31-Dec-2017), consistent with Youm7's stated Sept-2017 delivery target for this line. Neither World Bank document names the Mahmoudiya line specifically as 'completed'/'operating' (the ICR aggregates across six lines), so this is not a fully independent second confirmation of current operating status -- it corroborates existence, length, and the completion timeframe, but the 'operating' status rests primarily on the original Youm7 schedule plus the plausible inference that the line was in service on schedule (~2017) and feeds the Mahmoudiya power plant, which is itself an established operating station. No contradiction found; no source states the line was delayed, dropped, or is still under construction. Recommend medium tier pending a source that names this specific line as commissioned.

Same revived Youm7 source (Wayback 2020 capture, verified) is the only source found that itemizes SegmentCost = EGP 637 million specifically for this 52 km Mahmoudiya line, in a table listing per-line cost/length/delivery-date for six GASCO power-plant feeder lines (New Capital/Berlus/Beni Suef-Siemens 320 km @ EGP 3bn; Suez 3 km @ EGP 50m; South Helwan 1.2 km @ EGP 90m; 6th of October 0.4 km @ EGP 28m; Mahmoudiya 52 km @ EGP 637m; Damanhour 2.5 km @ EGP 82m). No contradiction found (the World Bank aggregate cost is consistent with, not contrary to, a ~637m EGP allocation to one of several lines), but corroboration is single-source -- flagging as medium tier rather than high.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solid. The Arab Gas Pipeline (AGP) Phase-1 Egyptian overland leg from El Arish (North Sinai, Mediterranean coast) across the Sinai peninsula to Taba (South Sinai, Gulf of Aqaba) is heavily documented; commissioned July 2003. Independently confirmed by offshore-technology.com (Verdict Media project page) and thenationalnews.com (2021 explainer), plus Wikipedia. Not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: correct - a high-pressure gas transmission trunk (36-in, cross-Sinai export trunk feeding the Taba->Aqaba subsea crossing and onward to Jordan/Syria/Lebanon), not gathering/process. DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate. P0436 is the 250 km Arish->Taba OVERLAND segment; the separate P7482 (Arab Gas Pipeline, Taba->Aqaba, 18 km) is the ~15 km subsea Gulf-of-Aqaba crossing - a legitimate sibling segment, not a double-count (RouteNotes 'IM: updated 2025 to reflect individual segment' documents the deliberate split). P0462 (Arish->Ashkelon, EMG line to Israel) shares the Arish origin but is a physically different pipeline. GulfPub lumps 'Arab Gas Pipeline | El Arish -> Aqaba' into one 169 km/36-in operating record - that corroborates existence/diameter/status but its 169 km is wrong (real Arish-Aqaba total ~265 km = 250 overland + ~15 subsea) and its operator 'East Mediterranean Gas Company' is a GulfPub confusion with the EMG (Arish-Ashkelon) company. ATTRIBUTION: GEM's Operator=Egyptian Natural Gas Co (GASCO) / Owner=Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co (EGAS) 100% is correct - offshore-technology names the Egyptian developer consortium as EGAS, ENPPI, Petrojet and GASCO. GulfPub's EMGC is wrong; prefer GEM. SPEC: length 250 km (overland), diameter 36 in, capacity 10.3 bcm/y (=360 bcf/y), start 2003, proposal 2001 - ALL corroborated by offshore-technology and The National (two independent origins; note offshore-technology and the sheet's hydrocarbons-technology ref are the same publisher, so I used The National as the second independent origin). Only weak point: SegmentCost 207,550,000 USD - the cited hydrocarbons-technology page no longer surfaces that number (existing_ref_check failed) and independent sources give the phase-1 investment as ~USD 220 million, so the exact 207.55M figure is unsupported; flagged for human, not auto-changed.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguous — this is the East Mediterranean Gas (EMG) El-Arish–Ashkelon subsea line, one of the most heavily documented pipelines in the region (Kingston Corp transaction dossier, Washington Institute, WorldOil, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Reuters, Wikipedia Arab Gas Pipeline). Real. CLASSIFICATION: correct — international gas transmission trunk (subsea, ~85 km offshore), not gathering/feeder/oil. Correctly on the gas tracker. DUPLICATE: no GEM duplicate in the 50-row Egypt roster; the Arab Gas Pipeline rows (P0436 Arish→South Sinai, P7482 Taba→Aqaba) are the onshore AGP that this line branches from, not the same pipe. GulfPub carries the counterpart 'Ashkelon - Arish Pipeline | operating | Ashkelon, Israel -> Arish, Egypt | op=EMGC' — confirms existence/endpoints/operator, but its dia=16in / len=62km / start=2015 are ALL wrong vs the corroborated 26in / 90km / 2008; a clean example of GulfPub Tier-2 specs not being authoritative. SPEC CONFIRMATIONS (all >=2 independent): length 90 km (Kingston '89 km, of which 85.4 km subsea'; Wikipedia AGP '90 km'); capacity 7 bcm/y (Kingston '7-9 BCM per year'; Wikipedia '7 bcm/y physical, 9 with upgrades'); start 2008 (Kingston 'started operation May 2008'); stop 2012 (Kingston 'ceased operation in 2012' — sabotage of the Sinai feeder began 2011, contract formally revoked Apr 2012, GEM's 2012 is defensible); reverse-flow restart 2020 (WorldOil/Al Jazeera 15 Jan 2020, Tamar+Leviathan). OWNER: EMG 61% / EMED 39% is correct — the EMED JV (East Gas 50%, Delek 25%, Noble 25%) bought 39% of EMG in Nov 2019 for ~USD520m (Algemeiner, Washington Institute); operator remains EMG. CAVEAT: the row mixes eras — StartYear1=2008 is the original Egypt→Israel export start, but Location (Ashkelon→Arish) and status=operating reflect the post-2020 reverse import of Israeli gas to Egypt. Endpoints/direction as shown match current operation, so acceptable, but worth a one-line ResearcherNotes note. NOTE also a 2023-2024 Gaza-war interruption (flows suspended Oct 2023, rerouted via Jordan, later resumed) — status=operating still correct as of 2025.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/SPEC: real, well-documented onshore gas transmission trunk in Egypt's Western Desert (Matruh governorate). Primary independent source: Egypt Oil & Gas magazine report 'The Western Desert: Egypt's Giant Petroleum Reservoir' (March 2020, issue 159) -- already the sheet's Diameter [ref] URL. NOTE the url_verifier substring screen FAILs on this URL for tokens like 'Obaiyed'/'Tarek' because the page actually serves a compressed PDF (content-type header says text/html but the bytes are a PDF stream) -- a documented ligature/PDF false-negative per url_verifier.py's own docstring. I fetched the PDF directly and extracted text with pdfplumber, which resolved this: p.4 of the extracted text contains a table 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert' with columns Pipeline | From | To | Length(Km) | Diameter(Inches) | Capacity(mmcf/d), and the row 'Obaiyed-Tarek Connector | Obaiyed/Salam Connector | Tarek | 49.5 | 32 | 600' -- an EXACT match to GEM's current Length=49.50km, Diameter=32in, Capacity=600.00 MMcf/d for this segment (segment_name in GEM's own backend is 'Obaiyed-Tarek Gas Pipeline', matching the table's 'Obaiyed-Tarek Connector'). Verified live (200) via `python scripts/url_verifier.py <url>` liveness-only mode; content match confirmed manually per the documented workaround. This is a SINGLE specific source (tier=medium, independent=false) -- I could not find a second independent source with matching segment-level specs (a 2004 Apache/Shell EIA describes the aggregate 34-inch 'Northern Gas Pipeline' network, not this specific 49.5km/32in leg; GulfPub's PE World Map lists the corridor as one aggregate 'Western Desert Gas Project - North Line' Obaiyed field->Ameriya Refinery, dia=34in, len=196km, op=BAPETCO -- a different level of granularity, not directly comparable to this segment, and itself only Tier-2). CLASSIFICATION confirmed: this is a legitimate gas transmission export line (not gathering/plant-internal), carrying sales gas from Khalda-concession fields toward the coast -- consistent across the 2004 Apache EIA ('A 34 inch gas export line handles all of the gas exported from the Khalda concession, Matrouh concession, Ras Kanayis concession, Ras El Hekma concession, Umbarka concession & South Umbarka concession') and the 2020 trade-press table. DUPLICATE check: P0474, P6687 ('Obaiyed Spurline', 41.5km/26in/480), and P3934 ('Tarek-Ameryia Gas Pipeline', 231km/34in/950) all share the identical pipeline_name 'Obaiyed-Amreya Northern Gas Pipeline' in GEM -- this LOOKS like a duplicate cluster at first glance, but the SAME Egypt Oil & Gas table lists all three as separate named legs with different from/to points and different specs (Tarek-Ameryia: Tarek->Ameryia 231/34/950; Obaiyed-Tarek Connector: Obaiyed/Salam Connector->Tarek 49.5/32/600; Obaiyed Spurline: Obaiyed->Obaiyed/Salam Connector 41.5/26/480), and the combined ~322km of the three legs closely matches an independent 2004 Oil & Gas Journal description of a single '315 km gas pipeline from Shell's Obaiyed concession to Egypt's gas grid.' Conclusion: legitimate segmentation of one corridor into three GEM rows, NOT an erroneous duplicate -- no merge recommended.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two separable issues found: (1) NAME/ENDPOINT MISMATCH -- GEM's own current sheet records StartLocation='Borg El Arab', EndLocation='Al ameryia', but the pipeline's own name references 'Midor' (the MIDOR/Middle East Oil Refinery) as if it were an endpoint, and neither field says 'Midor'. Of the two corroborating sources, only youm7 names 'Midor' explicitly (as a label in a project table, without further description); elwatannews describes the same 10km/24in spur without naming Midor at all, instead framing it as a distribution branch 'to meet the needs of Alexandria governorate and the northwest coast' -- a materially different characterization (city/network gas supply vs. a dedicated refinery feed) than 'a line to Midor' implies. (2) GEOGRAPHIC PLAUSIBILITY -- independently sourced coordinates put MIDOR refinery at approx. 31.0983N, 29.86311E (Global Energy Observatory geoid/6809, in the Amreya/Dekheila west-Alexandria industrial belt), whereas the well-known town/new city of 'Borg El Arab' (New Borg El Arab, en.wikipedia.org) sits roughly 25-30km further southwest/inland (~30.90-31.00N, 29.53-29.72E). A straight line between those two reference points is roughly 25-30km, not the ~10km the pipeline is recorded (and independently corroborated) as being. Either (a) 'Borg El Arab' in this pipeline's name/StartLocation refers to a nearer tie-in point within the same west-Alexandria industrial corridor as MIDOR/Amreya (plausible -- 'Borg El Arab' is also a large administrative qism/markaz of Alexandria Governorate that extends along the coast, not just the distant new city+airport), or (b) the 10km length is only the length of a short lateral tapping off the larger Amriya-El Alamein trunk near Borg El Arab, not a line spanning the whole Ameriya-to-Borg-El-Arab distance. Neither source disambiguates which reading is correct, so I am not proposing new Location values or asserting fabricated coordinates -- flagging for a human to resolve with a facility-level source (e.g., a MIDOR company disclosure or GASCO network map) if one becomes available. This does not undermine the length/diameter/cost corroboration in the companion validity entry, which held regardless of exactly which 'Borg El Arab' reference point is meant.

resolutions.recommendation: Fix Capacity: 6.8 is million CUBIC METRES/day, not MMcf/d. Convert to ~240 MMcf/d, or record 6.8 Mm3/d. Current 6.80 MMcf/d is wrong by ~35x.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/DUPLICATE: P6036 ('Pipeline 2') and its sibling P5132 ('Pipeline 1') are NOT a double-count of one pipe. Multiple independent trade sources confirm Zohr field is served by (at least) two physical 30-inch export trunklines to the El-Gamil onshore treatment plant near Port Said: the original line that came online with first commercial gas in Dec 2017, and a second 30-inch line added later as production ramped up (nsenergybusiness.com/offshore-technology.com describe 'Zohr I' and 'Zohr II', each ~216km; Offshore Magazine independently reports 'a new 30-in., 218-km pipeline, commissioned [Aug 2018]' tied to the T4 production-unit startup; Rigzone reports a Saipem contract addendum for a second 30-in export pipeline as part of the 'Ramp Up to Plateau' phase awarded ~Jan 2019). GEM's two-row model (Pipeline 1 / Pipeline 2 under one wiki page) is a reasonable way to represent this twin-line reality, not a duplicate. One nsenergybusiness passage even states the project includes 'three gas export pipelines, including two 30-inch pipelines' (Saipem's own project page mentions a '26-inch gas export trunkline' too) -- there may be a third physical line GEM hasn't captured, but that is a Discovery-workflow question, out of scope for this row-level audit; flagging for awareness only. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk (major offshore field-to-shore export line feeding the national grid via El-Gamil), not a gathering/process/plant-internal line -- confirmed. Sources used: nsenergybusiness.com/projects/zohr-gas-field-mediterranean-sea/, offshore-technology.com/marketdata/zohr-i-gas-pipeline-egypt/, offshore-technology.com/marketdata/zohr-ii-gas-pipeline-egypt/, offshore-mag.com/.../zohr-building-to-peak-gas-offshore-egypt, rigzone.com/.../offshore_egypt_project_to_start_new_phase-20-dec-2018-157768-article, ogj.com/.../zohr-pipeline-component-installation-offers-custom-deepwater-guidance, saipem.com/en/saipem-worldwide-projects/gas-field-offshore-zohr. Current status also independently reconfirmed as active/operating into 2025-2026 (Zohr field still producing ~2.7-3.2 bcfd, new wells being brought online in 2025-2026 per egyptoil-gas.com and ecofinagency.com), even though the sheet's current Status [ref] (nsenergybusiness) technically failed the automated 'operating' string check.

The actual, independently and repeatedly confirmed Shorouk-concession/Zohr partners are Eni 50%, Rosneft 30% (since Oct 2017 stake sale), BP 10%, Mubadala Petroleum/Energy 10% (since June 2018 stake sale) -- field/pipeline OPERATOR is Petrobel (Belayim Petroleum Co), a 50:50 Eni/EGPC joint venture, distinct from the ownership percentages. (2) marefa.org Arabic encyclopedia entry خط أنابيب الجميل-دمياط, itself citing the Egyptian Official Gazette petroleum-ministry land-acquisition decree of Nov 2016 (explicitly ‘قطر 42 بوصة' = diameter 42 inch), World-Bank funding, Petrojet's own project listing (‘AL-GAMIL/DAMIETTA (42"-50 KM)'), and Eni as EPC contractor — gives operator as Egyptian Natural Gas Holding/GASCO, owner as the Egyptian government, construction start 2016, and a turn-by-turn corridor. Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum (petroleum.gov.eg, MoP release 28 Dec 2022) and multiple independent trade/news outlets describe a two-phase GASCO project connecting the offshore Raven field (bp-operated, north Alexandria/Rashid area) to two destinations: Phase 1 (P6703 in this roster) = 70km/30in line to the Western Desert Gas Complex (WDGC), operational May 2021, capacity 350 MMcf/d; Phase 2 = a 5km/18in spur to the Al-Amiriya (Amreya) LPG/Butane Extraction Plant, launched 25 Sep 2022, capacity 100 MMcf/d, so that the Amreya butane plant could run at full design capacity. This 5km/18in spur is exactly P6704 -- length, diameter and both endpoint names (Rashid-area source, Ameriya/Alexandria destination) match precisely. Independent corroboration beyond the ministry release: Egypt Oil & Gas (trade press) 'El Molla Gives Green Light for Raven Field Gas Line to Al-Amirya Plant', attaqa.net (Arabic energy trade site) 2022-09-25 'مشروع ربط خط غاز حقل ريفين المصري يدخل مرحلته الثانية', youm7 2022-09-25 launch story, and EgyptToday's companion piece on the WDGC leg. These are genuinely separate outlets (ministry PR + Egyptian trade press + independent news), not one wire story reprinted -- tier high. The already-cited youm7 2023-07-10 article is a later, broader piece revisiting the whole Raven-connection project (mentions both the 70km and 5km legs and a planned 'Phase 3' WDGC capacity increase for Q3 2023); it is fine to keep as a secondary ref but is not the most precise source for this specific 5km/18in/Ameriya segment, which is why its automated content-check for the literal word 'operating' came back empty.
DUPLICATE check: NOT a duplicate of P6703 (Raven-Western Desert Cmplex Gas Pipeline, roster) -- that is the sibling 70km/30in/350 MMcf/d Phase-1 leg to the Western Desert Gas Complex; this row is the physically distinct 5km/18in/100 MMcf/d Phase-2 spur to the Amreya butane plant. Both legs stem from the same Raven-field connection project but are different pipe (different length, diameter, capacity, and destination) and are each entered once -- correctly split, not double-counted. Also checked against GulfPub's Egypt gas roster: GulfPub carries a separate 'Raven - Idku Pipeline' (bp, dia 16in, 46km, 2021) -- this is a THIRD, physically distinct line (Raven field to the Idku onshore gas/LNG complex, not to Amreya) and is not represented under P6704 or, as far as this roster shows, under any other GEM ProjectID in the Egypt gas operating set. That is a possible discovery gap worth a separate look, but it is not a duplicate concern for P6704 itself.
ATTRIBUTION: sheet Owner1 = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) 100%, identical to sibling P6703. All sources name GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company, an EGAS subsidiary) as the entity that built/owns/operates this specific line ('نفذته جاسكو' -- 'implemented by GASCO'). The GGIT schema has no separate Operator column, so recording the parent state holding company as Owner is the same convention used across this whole Egypt-gas sub-network (all EGAS-system rows) -- not treated as an error, but noting GASCO as the operating subsidiary for the record.
SPEC: Diameter 18in and Length 5.00km both match every source exactly. Capacity (currently blank in the sheet) is well-sourced at 100 MMcf/d and is staged as a fill below.

resolutions.recommendation: Correct LengthKnown (currently 405 km, no ref at all). Not one independent source supports anything near 405 km; two independent 2014-15 English trade-press sources on the exact project this row represents (DEKA = Denise-Karawan, operated by Petrobel/Eni/bp) put the real sealine lengths at 9 km (16-in) and 4 km (10-in), tying into an existing 32-in sealine network. 405 km would be roughly the length of the entire Egyptian Mediterranean coastline and is physically implausible for a subsea field tie-in only ~65 km offshore. Almost certainly a transcription artifact: the sheet's own cited 2012 Al-Mal (almalnews) source lists three Denise-project sealines as '3.7 km, 405 km, and 1 km' at 16in/16in/10in -- a lone 3-digit figure sandwiched between two single-digit ones, and no realistic subsea flowline of that length exists in this field. Recommend replacing with a sourced ~4-9 km figure (or marking length as unresolved/uncertain) rather than corroborating 405.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Chain: (1) GEM's own three refs checked -- petro-news.com/95212 is a generic '39 gas projects in Egypt' listicle; its only relevant passage is about the upstream 'Denise-Karawan field development' (5 wells, $578M) and never mentions a pipeline, length, or diameter. petro-news.com/8215 is a generic Petrobel company-history profile; no mention of Denise, Karawan, or any pipeline. almalnews.com/9021 (Al-Mal, 2012-11-10) is the only ref that actually gives numbers: 'the first [Denise] project includes laying offshore pipelines of length 3.7 km, 405 km, and 1 km, diameters 16in, 16in, and 10in respectively, to carry production from wells to new manifolds... the second project [Karawan] includes an 206 km, 10in offshore pipeline.' Both the 405 km and 206 km figures are outliers next to sub-5km neighbors in the same sentence and read as dropped-decimal artifacts (e.g. 4.05, 20.6). (2) Independent corroboration of the real project (bp/Eni 'DEKA' = Denise-Karawan, first gas Aug 2014): egyptoil-gas.com feature states 'Laying of 4 gas sealines (9 km 16" & 4 km 10") and relevant tie-ins to 32" existing sealine network,' well names Denise North West 1 / Denise North / Karawan / Denise South 6, Seth platform topside tie-in, Denise 70km offshore/~100m depth, Karawan 60km offshore/~68m depth. offshore-energy.biz ('Eni Starts Production from DEKA Project Offshore Egypt') independently corroborates: Temsah Concession, ~65 km north of Port Said, ~100m water depth, gas processed at El Gamil Gas Plant onshore, Denise South 6 first development well, Aug 2014 first gas at 1.8 MMcm/d + ~800 b/d condensate. Two independent modern trade sources agree closely (9km/4km sealines) and neither supports 405 km. (3) GulfPub's Egypt gas roster lists several distinct short Denise-area segments (Akhen-Denise 11km/16in, Denise-Wakar 15km/16in, Denise-Port Said 46km/16in, Denise-El Gamil 41km/16in, Zohr Export I/II to Denise 80km) -- none reaches 100km, let alone 405km, reinforcing that no real single Denise segment is this long. Diameter=16in is plausible/corroborated (matches both the almalnews 16in figure and egyptoil-gas's 9km/16in sealine) -- leaving that value alone.

resolutions.recommendation: Correct Owner/Parent company. Sheet currently lists Owner = Parent company = 'General Petroleum Company (GPC)'. GPC is a distinct, unrelated EGPC-group upstream company (Gulf of Suez fields, e.g. October field) with no stake in Petrobel. Petrobel's actual parents are the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) and Eni (via its Egyptian arm, historically AGIP/IEOC) -- confirmed by the sheet's own cited Operator source. Owner should read EGPC + Eni (or EGPC/IEOC), not GPC.
resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's own existing Operator ref (petro-news.com/8215, a Petrobel company-history profile, re-verified OK) states Petrobel was 'established under Law 16 of 1978 as an Egyptian joint-stock company between the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation [EGPC] and International Egyptian Oil Company [IEOC/AGIP-Eni's Egyptian subsidiary].' No mention of General Petroleum Company anywhere. Independently, gulfoilandgas.com's Petrobel supplier profile states 'PETROBEL is one of the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation companies jointly owned by ENI' -- a second, independent source agreeing EGPC+Eni, not GPC. resolutions.researcher_notes: The underlying infrastructure is real and operating: this row evidently represents (some segment of) the DEKA -- Denise/Karawan -- subsea gas development in the Temsah Concession, operated by Petrobel (Eni/bp/EGPC), which achieved first gas in August 2014 (Denise South 6 well, ~1.8 MMcm/d + ~800 b/d condensate) per two independent English trade-press sources (offshore-energy.biz, MEED). However, the sheet's current Status ref (petro-news.com/95212) is a generic '39 gas projects in Egypt' listicle article that never names 'Denise Gas Pipeline' and does not verify pipeline-specific operating status (url_verifier already flags it: '200 but data value not found'). resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solid. This is the subsea Gulf-of-Aqaba crossing of Arab Gas Pipeline Phase 1 (El Arish-Aqaba), inaugurated July 2003 by President Mubarak and King Abdullah II - which is exactly what the sheet's own Arabic ref (kingabdullah.jo, 'gas line between El Arish and Aqaba', ok=200) documents. Offshore-technology, Wikipedia and oilandgasadvancement all independently describe the '15km subsea pipeline from Taba to Aqaba' as a built, commissioned segment. Not phantom. CLASSIFICATION: correct - a gas transmission trunk (cross-border export line, not gathering/process/feeder; Fuel=Gas correct). DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate. P0436 (Arab Gas Pipeline, El Arish->'South Sinai', 250 km, 36 in) is the onshore Sinai overland segment El Arish->Taba; P7482 is the 15-18 km / 26 in subsea Taba->Aqaba crossing. They are complementary AGP Phase-1 segments deliberately split (RouteNotes 'IM: updated 2025 to reflect individual segment'), corroborated by sources that give 250 km onshore @36in + 15 km subsea @26in. GulfPub merges the whole Egyptian AGP into ONE feature (169 km, 36 in, El Arish->Aqaba) - i.e. GulfPub is the un-split version, not evidence of a GEM internal dup. Caveat: capacity 10.30 bcm/y is identical on P0436 and P7482 because it is the entire AGP nameplate (offshore-technology & Wikipedia both give 10.3 bcm/y for the line); correct as a per-segment throughput but must NOT be summed across segments. SPEC: Diameter 26 in CONFIRMED (Wikipedia + trade sources agree the subsea crossing is 26 in vs the 36 in onshore trunk). StartYear 2003 CONFIRMED (July 2003 commissioning, multiple independent sources). Capacity 10.3 bcm/y CONFIRMED as line design. LENGTH is the one discrepancy: GEM=18 km, but offshore-technology, oilandgasadvancement and Wikipedia all say 15 km for the Taba-Aqaba subsea segment - a ~20% overstatement; flag, do not silently pass.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/SPEC: real, gas transmission pipeline, confirmed. Read all three cited sources directly (not just the automated checker). dostor.org/4234553 (2022-11-18, 'بتوجيهات من الرئيس السيسى.. تطوير خط «إدكو- أبوحمص» لزيادة صادرات الغاز') states verbatim: 'وجرى تطوير خط فاز «ادكو- أبو حمص» في محافظة البحيرة، لتدعيم الشبكة القومية للقاز بطول ۳۰ كم وقطر ۴۲ بوصة، بتكلفة ۷۳۳ مليون جنيه' (the Idku-Abu Hummus line in Beheira governorate was developed to reinforce the national gas grid, 30km/42in, cost 733M EGP). egy-map.com (sourced 'from the official website of the Presidency') gives an identical description plus 'تاريخ التنفيذ فبراير ۲۰۲۰' (completion date Feb 2020) and status 'تم تنفيذه' (implemented/completed). petro-news.com/95212 (2024-10-10, a roundup of '39 gas projects in Egypt') repeats the identical 30km/42in/733M figures for the same named project. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: these three sources are NOT independent of each other -- all three trace to the same origin, the Egyptian Presidency's official megaprojects database/press material (egy-map explicitly cites 'نقلا من الموقع الرسمي لرئاسة الجمهورية'); this is one lineage restated three times, not 2+ independent corroborations, per the near-requirement. A genuinely separate origin -- GASCO's (Egyptian Natural Gas Company, Egypt's state gas-transmission grid operator) own official pipelines page -- surfaced in a Google search snippet describing 'Edco/Abu-Hommus gas pipeline is 29 km ... 42in diameter ... to transmit gas from north Alex fields ... capacity 35 MSCM/day ... scheduled to be completed and operational in July 2019', which corroborates length/diameter/existence from a second, non-Presidency-database source. However the live URL (http://www.gasco.com.eg/?page_id=5242) now fails to resolve (ConnectTimeout on http, SSLError on https -- site appears to have been restructured; the search engine still has the old page indexed) so it CANNOT be cited as a proposed_ref per the url_verifier requirement -- noting it here as uncited corroboration only, per the no-fabricated-URL rule. Net: length 30km (Presidency lineage) vs 29km (GASCO, uncited) is an immaterial ~3% variance; diameter 42in corroborated by two genuinely distinct origins -- confirmed. Classification (transmission, feeding the national gas grid from field-side production) is correct, not a gathering/plant-internal line. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 30-row Egypt-gas-operating roster and the 95-feature GulfPub Egypt list -- no other GEM row or GulfPub feature represents this specific Idku-to-Abu-Hummus corridor (the several other Idku-prefixed rows/features -- Idku-Tanta, Idku-Damietta, Rashid-Idku, Simian/Sienna-Idku, Fayoum-Idku -- are all different corridors/endpoints). No duplicate identified. Note for a future dedup pass: the project is explicitly described as an 'ازدواج' (doubling/twinning) of an existing corridor -- i.e. a second parallel pipe alongside a pre-existing line on the same route -- so if GEM ever captures the original (pre-2020) single line under a different name, that would need reconciling against this row; no such row was found in the current roster/GulfPub list, so not flagged as an active duplicate now. Automated ref-checker false negatives worth noting (not real problems): the SegmentCost check flagged '733,000,000' as 'not found' on egy-map.com because the page spells the value as '۷۳۳ مليون جنيه' (733 million pounds, not digit-string '733000000'); the ConstructionYear check similarly flagged '2020' as 'not found' because the page uses Arabic-Indic digits '۲۰۲۰' rather than ASCII '2020'. Both values ARE present on manual read.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Read the full raw text of the cited dostor.org/4234553 article directly (WebFetch was blocked by a 403, so fetched via curl with a browser UA and parsed the HTML). The article covers TWO separate projects in one piece: (1) 'the Idku-Abu Hummus gas LINE ... 30km/42in, cost 733M EGP' (the pipeline row this shard covers), and separately (2) 'كما تم تطوير مصنع إدكو لإسالة القاز الطبيعي' (the Idku NATURAL GAS LIQUEFACTION PLANT was also developed). The article then states verbatim, describing the LNG PLANT specifically: 'يعمل على مصنع إسالة القاز الطبيعي بإدكو عدد من الشركات وهي الهينة العامة للبترول بنسبة ۱۲%، والشركة المصرية القابضة للقازات الطبيعية "إيجاس" ۱۲%، وشركة بريتش جاز التى استحوذت عليها شركة شل ۳۵.۵%، وشركة بتروناس الماليزية ۳۵.۵%، وشركة إنجى الفرنسية ... ۵%' (the Idku LNG liquefaction plant has several companies working on it: EGPC 12%, EGAS 12%, British Gas [acquired by Shell] 35.5%, Petronas 35.5%, Engie [formerly Gaz de France] 5%). Those exact five owners and exact percentages are what GEM has attached to the PIPELINE row (Owner1='General Petroleum Co' 12%, Owner2='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' 12%, Owner3='British Gas' 35.5%, Owner4='Petronas' 35.5%, Owner5='Engie SA' 5%) -- i.e. the ownership structure of a wholly separate asset (the LNG export terminal) has been copy-pasted onto this domestic 30km transmission spur. Independently corroborated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edku confirms the Idku LNG plant is 'jointly owned by Shell and Petronas' -- the same two majority owners, describing the LNG plant specifically, with no mention of pipeline ownership. The pipeline itself is explicitly a national-gas-grid reinforcement project attributed to Ministry of Petroleum/Presidency directives, which in Egypt's sector structure is normally built/operated by GASCO (Egyptian Natural Gas Company), not by the offshore-field/LNG-plant JV partners -- but I could not find a source naming GASCO specifically for THIS pipeline (only its general remit over the national grid), so I am not proposing a replacement owner value, just flagging the current one as wrong.

resolutions.recommendation: FuelSource 'Idku Oil Fields' should read 'Idku gas fields' (or similar) -- every source describing this project calls it a gas line moved gas produced from Idku's GAS fields; none mentions oil.
resolutions.researcher_notes: dostor.org and egy-map.com both state the project's purpose as 'نقل القاز المنتج من حقول إدكو' (transporting the gas produced from Idku FIELDS -- حقول = fields, no qualifier of 'oil'; the whole subject of the sentence and the source document is natural gas). GASCO's own description (search-snippet only, uncited live) calls the source 'north Alex[andria] fields', i.e. the North Alexandria/West Delta Deep Marine gas concessions that come onshore at Idku -- again gas, not oil. 'Idku Oil Fields' as currently written appears to be a mislabeling.

The article's PUBLISH date appears to have been mistaken for a project START year. egy-map.com (sourced from the Presidency's own project database) explicitly gives 'тاريخ التنفيذ فبراير ۲۰۲۰' (completion/implementation date: February 2020) -- recommend StartYear1 ≈ 2020 instead, sourced to egy-map.com; reconsider whether ConstructionYear (currently also 2020, same source) and StartYear1 should be two different years or are duplicating one data point.

This is consistent with GASCO's own (uncited, dead-link) corporate description that the line was 'scheduled to be completed and operational in July 2019' -- both independently point to a 2019-2020 in-service window, not 2022. Read the full dostor.org article body directly and it contains no year other than the implicit publish date (2022-11-18) and no explicit project-start/completion year at all -- it is a generic 'the Ministry has done a lot under Sisi's directives' piece, so citing it for StartYear1=2022 looks like a date-of-publication/date-of-event conflation.

resolutions.recommendation: Rename row to 'Karawan Gas Pipeline' (or similar), correct StartLocation/EndLocation region from 'Western Desert' to offshore Temsah Concession / East Nile Delta (Mediterranean, near Port Said) — NOT Western Desert — and re-verify Owner (probably not '100% General Petroleum Co').
resolutions.researcher_notes: This row is misidentified. GEM's own gem.wiki page (https://www.gem.wiki/Qarun_Gas_Pipeline, read for leads only, not cited) gives the pipeline's Arabic name as انبوب فاز حقل كروان = 'gas pipeline of the Karawan field' (كروان = Karawan), NOT قارون (Qarun) — these are two unrelated Arabic words that were conflated in translation. 'Qarun' is a real, well-documented, entirely distinct entity: Qarun Petroleum Company (QPC) is an EGPC/Apache Corporation joint venture producing OIL in the Qarun concession, Western Desert (verified: gulfoilandgas.com/webpro1/prod1/suppliercat.asp?sid=2806, contains 'Qarun' + 'Apache' — OK); QPC's own real pipeline is a 45 km, 16-inch OIL line to Dahshour, nothing like this row's 206 km/10 in gas spec. 'Karawan' (كروان), by contrast, is an offshore Mediterranean gas field in the Temsah Concession (East Nile Delta, ~60 km off Port Said, ~68 m water depth), developed jointly with the Denise field under Eni/BP's 'DEKA' (Denise-Karawan) project, operated by the Petrobel joint venture (Petrobel = Belayim Petroleum Company — matches this row's Operator field). Independent English trade press (egyptoil-gas.com DEKA feature, verified OK; offshore-mag.com DEKA article, verified OK) confirms: 'The DEKA project launched by Petrobel is targeting the development of both the Denise and Karawan fields' in the 'Temsah Concession located at offshore Egypt.' The sheet's own existing Length/Diameter ref (almalnews.com/9021, verified OK, contains 'كروان' and '206') explicitly attaches the 206 km/10 in figures to the KARAWAN project, not Qarun — confirming the data values were pulled correctly but the identity/name/location were not. This also means the row's Status/Fuel/PipelineType ref (petro-news.com/95212/, a roundup of '39 gas projects in Egypt') does not mention Qarun OR Karawan by name at all (checked directly — lists 8 unrelated trunk lines: Idku-Abu Hamsa, Nobaria-Mit Nama, Dahshur-Al Wasati, Tina-Abu Sultan, New Capital-Dahshur, Nors-Abu Madi-El Gamil, Nobaria-Sadat, Gamsa-Finosa), matching the worklist's own automated flag ('200 but data value not found'). Net: the underlying pipe (a Karawan-field subsea sealine tying into the existing 32-inch Denise/Temsah export network to El Gamil) does physically exist and is well corroborated — but under the WRONG name and WRONG location in this GEM row. Owner is also suspect: 'General Petroleum Co (GPC)' is a different EGPC subsidiary (Gulf of Suez-oriented); the Temsah Concession / DEKA project is a 50/50 Eni-BP interest operated via Petrobel — GPC as 100% owner does not match any source found and should be re-verified, not left as-is.

resolutions.recommendation: Re-verify the 206 km length against DEKA project engineering literature before treating it as confirmed; likely too long by an order of magnitude for a field-to-existing-line tie-in at this distance offshore.
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's Length=206 km / Diameter=10 in traces to almalnews.com/9021 (Arabic), which states the Karawan project pipeline is 'بطول 206 كم وقطر 10 بوصات' (206 km long, 10 in diameter) tying into the existing 32-inch sealine. That is the ONLY source for this number, and it is a single, non-independently-corroborated figure (tier=low per the confidence rubric — no second source agrees). It is also hard to reconcile with the physical geography and with independent English technical trade coverage of the same DEKA project: the Karawan field itself is only ~60 km off the Egyptian coast (egyptoil-gas.com DEKA feature, verified OK), and that same feature states the ENTIRE DEKA project (both Denise and Karawan fields combined) laid only '4 gas sealines (9 km 16" & 4 km 10") and relevant tie-ins to [the] 32" existing sealine network' — i.e. a maximum of ~13 km of new small-diameter sealine project-wide, not 206 km for Karawan alone. A 206 km, 10-inch tie-in from a field only ~60 km offshore is not plausible as described. Possible explanations: a decimal-point transcription error in the original Arabic source (e.g. 20.6 km), a mix-up with a cumulative/different length figure, or conflation with the separately-listed Denise-project figures (3.7 km, 405 km, 1 km) from the same almalnews article (GEM already has a 'Denise Gas Pipeline', P7447, at 405 km/16in from this same article — also worth an independent re-check, as 405 km is equally implausible for a ~70 km-offshore tie-in). Recommend treating 206 km as unresolved/low-confidence pending a second, independent source (e.g. an SPE/OnePetro engineering paper on DEKA) rather than confirmed.

resolutions.pipeline_name: New Administration Capital PS Gas Pipeline
resolutions.recommendation: Keep as a distinct row (existence + classification hold up); the Status/Cost ref check failures are just verifier string-matching against a spelled-out Arabic number, not a real problem with the source.
resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's sole source, petro-news.com/95212/ (an achievements-style roundup titled '39 projects.. map of natural gas projects in Egypt', dated 2024-10-10), lists this exact project as item #23, titled 'Khatt Taghdhiya Mahattat Kahraba' al-'Asima al-Idariya' (feed line for the New Administrative Capital power station): the text reads (in translation) 'the project comes as part of the urgent plan to supply the Siemens power station with natural gas, via a 32-inch feed line, 63 km long, at a cost of 327 million EGP.' That is an exact match on length (63 km), diameter (32 in) and cost (327M EGP) to the GEM row, and it is explicitly framed as an URGENT/interim measure to get gas to the Siemens-built New Capital combined-cycle plant. Re-verified live: url_verifier OK 200, page text contains '63'/'32'/'327'. GASCO (the Egyptian Natural Gas Company) is independently confirmed via a live, verified source (youm7.com, 2016-04-03) to be the entity building gas feed lines plus pressure-reduction/measurement stations for exactly the New Capital / Beni Suef / Burullus Siemens mega power plants (~3bn EGP investment program), which supports this being a genuine GASCO grid-reinforcement project rather than a phantom entry. PipelineType=transmission is reasonable for a 32in/63km trunk-grade line even though its sole consumer is one power plant -- consistent with how GEM already classifies sibling New-Capital feed lines (P3930 Dahshur-New Capital 70km/32in, P3366 Tineh-Abu Sultan-New Capital 165km/42in). Status=operating is not literally stated in the source (no explicit 'operational' wording), but the article is an achievements/completed-projects roundup (published 2024, describing the project in the past/completed tense with a fixed final cost), and the New Capital plant itself has been commercially operating since roughly 2019, so 'operating' is a reasonable read -- flagging as a caveat rather than upgrading to a hard confirm. Fuel=Gas and Location=Egypt/Egypt are trivially correct. resolutions.researcher_notes: The gem.wiki page's 9 backlinked citations all point to ONE Argaam article (id/1058075). At first glance the article's headline only names the ‘Al-Noubareya–Al-Sadat’ line, which looked like a possible misattribution (i.e. the Edfu row citing a source that is actually about a different pipeline, P3928). Fetched the article with a browser UA (the bare curl fetch without a UA returns a broken ASP.NET error page — a liveness false-negative, not proof the source is dead) and confirmed the real article headline and body cover TWO lines announced together on 2014-10-03: 'النوبارية–السادات' (73km/36in) AND 'خط إدفو' (Edfu line). The Edfu paragraph reads (translated): 'the Edfu gas line, 37 km long and 12 inches in diameter, was completed at a cost of EGP 95 million, to deliver natural gas to sugar and paper factories as well as homes in the city of Edfu' — an exact match to GEM's Length=37km, Diameter=12in, SegmentCost=95,000,000 EGP. The digit-substring screen failed on Status ('operating' not literal — expected, status is inferable: a completed/inaugurated supply line) and on SegmentCost (article writes '95 مليون جنيه' in words, not digits) — both are content false-negatives, not real problems; I read the page directly and both values are supported. Traced the article's origin: Argaam explicitly bylines it as reprinted from Al-Shorouk (الشروق المصرية); found the original Shorouk News article (same date, same content) and a third reprint on emiratesvoice.com — all three trace to the same Oct-2014 Petroleum Ministry report to Minister Sherif Ismail, so per the standing corroboration rule these do NOT count as independent of each other (one origin, three reprints). For a genuinely separate line of evidence: (1) Misr Edfu Paper Company is a real, independently documented paper mill at Edfu (trade press), corroborating the article's stated purpose (gas to feed the paper/sugar factories); (2) a 2025-09-12 Youm7 report (unrelated outlet, unrelated date, does not cite the 2014 story) describes a fire on 'one of the natural gas lines' in Edfu city, confirming a live/operating gas pipeline presence in Edfu 11 years after the 2014 completion — consistent with Status=operating but without matching Length/Diameter specifics. Classification: PipelineType=transmission is consistent with GEM convention for other small-diameter (10–24in), short (30–50km) GASCO/Khalda supply spurs in this same roster (e.g. P6689 Abu Sennan Spur 45km/14in, P7580 Mahmoudiah PS 52km) — these are dedicated high-pressure trunk feeders off the national grid, not in-town low-pressure distribution mains, so 'transmission' is not a misclassification. Duplicate check: compared against the South Valley/'Upper Egypt' Gas Pipeline trunk (GEM P0477, Dahshour→Aswan, 930km, 30–36in — independently confirmed via a 2010 inauguration article and the EIB project page, which describe the trunk terminating AT Aswan city) and against GulfPub's Egypt roster (no 'Edfu'-named entry). At 12in/37km the Edfu line is far too small and short to be a re-entry of the 930km trunk; it reads as a distinct terminal extension/spur south of the Aswan grid terminus into Edfu (via or near Kom Ombo, where Arabic-language sources independently describe a natural-gas pressure-reduction/metering station serving Edfu, Kom Ombo and Nasr al-Nuba villages) — not a duplicate. Operator: GEM's 'Egyptian Natural Gas Co' matches the article's naming of GASCO ('شركة جاسكو') as the operator reporting on/implementing this reinforcement project. Net: real pipeline, correctly classified, not a duplicate, specs and operator match the cited (if single-origin) source — caveat only on source independence for the numeric fills, hence tier medium not high.
