resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints Dahshour and Aswan confirmed by independent sources; waypoints are the named phase-boundary towns (Beni Suef, Abu Qurqas/Minya, Asyut, Sohag, Girga) from petroleumafrica/OGJ/EIB. Coordinates are real place centroids from general geographic knowledge, not fabricated pipe surveys; no coordinate invented for an unnamed point. Route accuracy 'high' is consistent with the sourced corridor at network granularity.

resolutions.start_name: El Tina / Tina Bay area, Port Said Governorate (GASCO East-Mediterranean gas receiving/metering point)
resolutions.end_name: Mit Nema, Qalyub markaz, Al Qalyubia Governorate

waypoints.name: Sharqia Governorate transit corridor (unsourced intermediate point)

resolutions.corridor_desc: Sourced Egyptian government/media reporting consistently names the corridor as GASCO's 'El Tina West / Mit Nema' national-grid trunk, carrying East Mediterranean offshore gas (Zohr/Nooros-era) from the El Tina area east of Port Said generally south-southwest across the eastern Nile Delta (through Sharqia Governorate, unconfirmed exact alignment) into Al Qalyubia Governorate, terminating at Mit Nema village (Qalyub markaz) -- a documented multi-line GASCO grid junction (a separate 'El Noubareya-Mit Nema' line, matching GEM P3346, also ties in there from the west). No route GeoJSON, KMZ, or as-built alignment map was located; the corridor above is inferred only from named endpoints and purpose statements in press/ministry sources, not a surveyed centerline -- treat as a loose bound, not a precise route. The El Tina start coordinate given is the broader 'Tina Bay/Plain' locality (a documented geographic feature east of Port Said city); the exact GASCO facility footprint within that area is not independently pinned down.
resolutions.researcher_notes: End coordinate (Mit Nema village) is a specific, independently sourced named-place match to the sheet's EndLocation. Start coordinate is a defensible but looser proxy for the named 'El Tina' area (Tina Bay/Plain, a documented geographic feature east of Port Said) rather than a pinned facility. No intermediate waypoints could be sourced, so RouteAccuracy is not upgraded beyond medium -- this is a corridor suggestion for a human routes-repo pass, not a route replacement.

resolutions.start_name: El Noubareya (Al Nubaria), Beheira Governorate
resolutions.end_name: Mit Nema, Qalyub, Al Qalyubia Governorate

waypoints.name: North Giza power station (El Kata, Monshaet El Qanater, Giza) - intermediate delivery point per WB ESIA / GASCO 2015 statement

resolutions.corridor_desc: Per the 2011 World Bank ESIA for this project ('Nubaria-Metnama Natural Gas Pipeline'), the route starts near Nubaria power station in Beheira, runs south along the El Rayah El Nasry drain, cuts east into the North Giza power station intake, then continues across agricultural land in the heart of the Nile Delta (crossing major roads, canals, and the Nile itself via tunneling) before terminating at Nawa/Ezbet Swelem near Mit Nema in Qalyubia. This gives a defensible Beheira -> Giza -> Qalyubia corridor consistent with the sheet's StartState/Province=Behara and EndState/Province=Al Qalyubia. Caveats: the start coordinate given is the general Al Nubaria town centroid (not the specific power-station pipeline chamber the ESIA describes as the true start, which I could not independently pin); the end coordinate is carried over from the sheet's existing RouteNotes Google Maps pin (30.145278,31.234444) - I confirmed independently only that Mit Nema is a village in Qalyub district, Al Qalyubia Governorate (per marefa.org), which is geographically consistent with that pin, but I did not re-derive or independently verify the exact coordinate myself, so it should be read as presumed/plausible rather than freshly sourced.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Corridor and named waypoints (Nubaria area -> North Giza power station -> Mit Nema/Qalyubia via the delta) are well sourced from the WB ESIA and corroborated by shbketmsr24's independent GASCO statement. Endpoint coordinates are town/facility-level approximations (Al Nubaria centroid; North Giza power plant from globalenergyobservatory.org, not gem.wiki), not survey-grade pipeline chamber locations - I did not fabricate any coordinate; where I lacked independent confirmation (the Mit Nema pin) I explicitly flagged the figure as carried over/presumed rather than freshly verified.

resolutions.pipeline_name: El Tina- Abu Sultan- New Administrative Capital Gas Pipeline
resolutions.start_name: El Tina / Qantara East area, Port Said Governorate (GASCO gas junction on the Suez Canal's east bank, near the Tina Plain)
resolutions.end_name: New Administrative Capital power station area, east of Cairo (Phase 2 ties into the 'Hot Tap of Dahshour Pipeline' at the New Capital)

waypoints.name: Abu Sultan, Ismailia Governorate (phase boundary: 92 km from El Tina; 73 km on to the New Capital tie-in per Petrojet's own project breakdown)

resolutions.corridor_desc: Two-phase GASCO trunk built by Petrojet: Phase 1 runs ~92 km from a valve/tie-in point at El Tina (on the Suez Canal's east bank in Port Said Governorate, in the Tina Plain / Qantara East area) south through Ismailia Governorate to Abu Sultan (23 HDD crossings along the way, per Petrojet). Phase 2 continues ~73 km from Abu Sultan west/southwest to a hot-tap tie-in with the existing Dahshour Pipeline at the New Administrative Capital, east of Cairo (11 HDD crossings). Total 165 km across Port Said, Ismailia, and Cairo governorates -- note GEM's own Location fields only record Port Said (start) and Cairo (end) and omit the Ismailia governorate the line actually transits via Abu Sultan. I have HIGH confidence in this waypoint order and the 92km/73km split (Petrojet, the constructing contractor) and in the 3 governorates (government source + Petrojet), but LOW confidence in precise point coordinates: I did NOT use the specific valve-room coordinates in an EIB/PETROSAFE 2005 EIA document that also covers an 'El Tina-Abu Sultan' corridor, because that document is for a different, older (32in/60km, Ataqa-power-station-feed) pipeline, not this one -- reusing its coordinates here would misattribute a different asset's surveyed route to P3366. The single coordinate I did supply (New Administrative Capital, ~30.02N/31.74E) is general public-geography knowledge of the New Capital's location east of Cairo, not sourced from a pipeline-specific document -- treat as a loose bound, not a surveyed point. El Tina and Abu Sultan are left uncoordinated (null) rather than guessed.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Waypoint order and km split from Petrojet's own (non-citable, JS-rendered) project page; governorates from the citable government-sourced cluster. No coordinates fabricated -- New Capital point is loose public-geography knowledge, El Tina/Abu Sultan left null. A human routes-repo pass should locate the actual GASCO valve rooms/hot-tap point via satellite imagery or a GASCO GIS source before any route is added.

resolutions.start_name: El Gamil, Port Said Governorate
resolutions.end_name: El Arish, North Sinai Governorate

waypoints.name: El-Tena East / El Tina Sharkiya valve room (Suez Canal east bank crossing point)
Roman compressor station
Bir El-Abd

resolutions.corridor_desc: El Gamil (Port Said governorate, Mediterranean coast) -> ~41 km inland/south to a crossing beneath the Suez Canal near El-Tina Sharkiya/El-Qantara East (per youm7, 2011) -> the GASCO 'Abr Sinai' onshore corridor runs east-southeast through North Sinai via Roman compressor station and Bir El-Abd -> El Arish (per EIB EIA, 2007, which gives explicit coordinates for the El-Tena East start point, Roman station, Bir El-Abd, and the El Arish end point of its 111 km El-Tena East->El-Arish segment). NOTE on the coordinates: the EIB document's own 'long.'/'lat.' labels appear transposed relative to actual geography (values it labels 'long.' fall in the 31-degree range typical of Sinai latitudes, and values it labels 'lat.' fall in the 32-34-degree range typical of Sinai longitudes); I have swapped them below to match known town locations (El Qantara East ~30.9N/32.3E, Bir el-Abd town ~31.0N/33.0E, El Arish city ~31.13N/33.80E all land within a few km of the corrected points), and flag this transposition explicitly rather than silently using the document's literal labels.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoint city coordinates for El Gamil (a documented named landmark/former airfield in Port Said governorate) and El Arish are general-area, publicly known town/landmark coordinates, not tied to an exact valve-room location -- used only because no single source gives a precise El Gamil interconnection point. The three intermediate waypoints ARE tied to specific named GASCO facilities with EIB-sourced coordinates (with the lat/lon transposition correction noted above). No coordinate here was invented: every point is either a defensible named-place location or a corrected transcription of a primary-source coordinate. Given the transposition issue and the fact that the El Gamil->Suez-Canal segment relies on a single weaker (Arabic news, no coordinates) source, I recommend 'medium' rather than the current 'high' RouteAccuracy pending a cleaner primary source for the El Gamil segment specifically.

resolutions.start_name: El Noubareya (Nubaria), Beheira governorate
resolutions.end_name: Sadat City (Madinat as-Sadat), Monufia governorate
resolutions.corridor_desc: The line runs from the El Nubaria grid node in northwestern Beheira governorate southeastward across the western Nile-Delta fringe / desert-edge toward Sadat City in Monufia governorate — a national-grid transmission link carrying gas from northern high-pressure production (Burullus, Abu Qir) via Sadat City onward toward Dahshour to feed the North Cairo / Abu Rawash / South Cairo power stations. Endpoint cities are firmly named by sources; the intervening corridor is not mapped, so the bound is loose (corridor is the ~50-70 km straight-line band between the two named cities, route length 73 km). Coordinates are city-centroid approximations for the two named endpoints, NOT surveyed pipeline vertices. egy-map's single map-center coordinate (~30.59N, 31.51E) plots near Qalyubia, inconsistent with a Nubaria->Sadat alignment, so it was NOT used.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named cities in presidency.eg (Nubaria->Sadat) and egy-map (end governorate Menoufia). Coordinates are defensible city-centroid approximations (El Nubaria ~30.68N/30.10E in Beheira; Sadat City ~30.378N/30.502E in Monufia) — flagged approximate, not surveyed. No coordinates fabricated; egy-map's inconsistent map-center point was deliberately rejected. Intervening vertices unknown; corridor bound is loose.

resolutions.start_name: El Wasta, Beni Suef Governorate, Egypt
resolutions.end_name: Beni Suef Thermal Power Plant (Ghayadah, near Biba, Beni Suef Governorate)
resolutions.corridor_desc: Loosely bounded only. Named endpoints are reasonably solid: El Wasta town (start, per egy-map.com and the WB 9-pipeline list) and the Beni Suef thermal power plant / decompression station, located near the village of Ghayadah east of Biba town center, Beni Suef Governorate (end, per egy-map.com purpose statement and WB ESIA item #3). El Wasta and Biba/Ghayadah are only ~45-50 km apart on a direct Nile-valley line, well short of the pipeline's stated 65 km, so the true corridor must deviate – most plausibly it continues the pattern documented for the adjacent, well-sourced Dahshour–El Wasta segment (which runs on the DESERT side, west of the Nile, paralleling the Cairo–Fayoum road then the Western Cairo–Asyut desert road, rather than through the populated floodplain) south from El Wasta to a decompression station within the Beni Suef power-plant complex. I could not find a source describing THIS segment's specific route (as opposed to the sibling segment's), so this is an inferred extension of a documented pattern, not a sourced path – no waypoints are asserted, and end coordinates are the nearest town (Biba) rather than the plant itself, since I could not independently source the plant's precise coordinates (a GEM wiki page exists for 'Beni Suef power plant' but per standing rules GEM cannot be cited/used as the coordinate source).
resolutions.researcher_notes: start_lat/lon for El Wasta town and end_lat/lon for Biba town (nearest named place to the Beni Suef power plant/decompression station) sourced from db-city.com gazetteer coordinates (non-GEM, independent of the pipeline sources); NOT the plant's own coordinates, which I could not independently confirm outside of GEM's own wiki page (excluded per standing rules). No coordinates fabricated – no waypoints given since no source describes the actual routed path for this specific segment (only the sibling Dahshour–El Wasta segment's route is documented).

resolutions.start_name: Dahshur gas tie-in/distribution point, Giza Governorate (GASCO national-grid hub near Dahshur town, corridor shared with the South Valley Gas Pipeline and Dahshur–Mostorod line)
resolutions.end_name: New Administrative Capital – Siemens combined-cycle power plant supply zone, Cairo Governorate (New Capital 'power plant zone', east of the New Capital's downtown/government district along the Katameya–Ain Sokhna corridor)

waypoints.name: El Katameya (New Cairo), Cairo Governorate -- confirmed waypoint: Al-Ahram's 2017 court report states the decreed route runs 'in front of' Suez Cement Co.'s factory at Qattamiya

resolutions.corridor_desc: Al-Ahram's court report (decree 717/2016) places the route across Cairo and Giza governorates and explicitly names El Katameya (Qattamiya), southeast Cairo along the Cairo–Ain Sokhna corridor, as a point the line passes through/near (it runs in front of Suez Cement's Katameya plant, which triggered the land-seizure dispute). Egy-map/Presidency source confirms the line's purpose is to feed the New Administrative Capital's Siemens power station, sited ~42km east of Cairo off the Katameya–Ain Sokhna road. Combined with the pipeline name itself ('New Administrative Capital–Dahshur'), the most defensible corridor is: Dahshur (Giza, west bank GASCO grid tie-in) -> crosses the Nile/greater Cairo southern periphery -> El Katameya/Ain Sokhna Road corridor (confirmed waypoint) -> New Administrative Capital power-plant zone. I could not independently source the power plant's exact coordinates (no official lat/lon published in the sources checked), so the eastern endpoint given is the New Capital's general downtown/government-district coordinate, not the precise plant gate -- treat it as an approximate anchor, not a precise tie-in point. Start/waypoint coordinates are standard, well-documented locations for Dahshur town and El Katameya district, not fabricated.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from GEM's own pipeline name (Dahshur, Giza -> New Administrative Capital, Cairo) plus the litigation source's route detail (Cairo/Giza governorates, passing El Katameya) and the egy-map/Presidency source's stated purpose (feeding the New Capital's Siemens power station). No coordinates were invented: Dahshur and El Katameya are well-known named localities; the New Capital endpoint is given only as the general downtown/government-district area since the specific power-plant gate coordinates were not found in any source I could verify. Suggested accuracy raised from 'low' to 'medium' on the strength of one independently-confirmed waypoint (Katameya) and named, governorate-bounded endpoints -- not to 'high' because the precise plant tie-in point and the exact pipe corridor between Dahshur and Katameya remain unsourced.

resolutions.start_name: Amriya (Al-Amiriya), Alexandria Governorate
resolutions.end_name: New Alamein City, Matrouh Governorate
resolutions.corridor_desc: Runs WSW from the Amriya gas/industrial hub (SW Alexandria) along or near the Alexandria-Marsa Matruh coastal corridor (International Coastal Road / North Coast strip) to New Alamein City on the Mediterranean, per Daily News Egypt's description ('from the Amiriya area in Alexandria to New Alamein') and the Ministry of Petroleum's grouping of it with a Borg El Arab spur. No independently sourced intermediate waypoints were found (no GIS trace, no named intermediate towns beyond Borg El Arab, which belongs to the separate 10km spur/P6032, not this trunk) -- endpoints are reasonably well anchored (named city/district coordinates), but the exact path between them is not sourced beyond 'follows the coastal corridor'. Length disagreement (120-170km reported vs GEM's 130km) means the true routing could be less direct / more winding than a straight endpoint-to-endpoint line would imply.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoint coordinates are for the named places (Al-Amiriya district centroid; New Alamein city centroid, per public place-coordinate lookups), not for the pipeline itself -- no pipeline-specific coordinates were found or fabricated. Also note: the sheet's existing RouteNotes URL (masrawy.com, 2021/3/6) is truncated/malformed and returns HTTP 400 on verification -- it appears to be the Arabic-language report of the same March-2021 ministerial inspection Daily News Egypt covered in English, but the URL itself is broken and should be fixed or replaced, not relied on as-is.

resolutions.start_name: Nooros field (offshore, Abu Madi West development license, Nile Delta)
resolutions.end_name: El Gamil gas treatment plant / national-grid tie-in, Port Said Governorate

waypoints.name: Abu Madi gas treatment plant, Belkas area, Dakahlia Governorate

resolutions.corridor_desc: Two onshore-tie-in segments, both stated to be onshore pipe ('خط بري' - land line) despite the field itself being offshore: (1) Nooros field (offshore Nile Delta, shallow water, ~120km NE of Alexandria, part of the Abu Madi West license operated by Petrobel) comes ashore and connects to the Abu Madi gas treatment plant, a long-established Petrobel/Eni processing hub in the northern part of Dakahlia Governorate (near Belkas); (2) from Abu Madi the line continues east/north-east across the eastern Nile Delta to the El Gamil gas treatment plant near Port Said, where gas is processed and injected into the national grid. This matches the GEM start/end administrative fields (Dakahlia -> Port Said) and the sheet's own RouteNotes description. I could not source defensible precise coordinates for either treatment plant or the Nooros wellhead/landfall point from a page I could independently fetch and verify (a websearch synthesis surfaced apparent coordinates for 'Abu Madi Gas Field' and 'El Gamil Plant' but I could not confirm them against a live, fetchable primary source, and a wikimapia page for El Gamil returned only a stub), so all lat/lon are left null per the no-fabrication rule. The corridor is well-bounded at the named-place level (Belkas/Dakahlia -> El Gamil/Port Said, ~130km per the Ministry source) but not at coordinate precision.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints and the intermediate Abu Madi tie-in are all named and independently sourced (sheet's own sfegypt.com ref plus offshore-technology.com and egyptoil-gas.com), replacing the dead petrojeteg.com RouteNotes link with live corroborating sources describing the same corridor. No coordinates were fabricated; the dead petrojeteg.com?project=2207 URL currently in RouteNotes returns a connection error (DNS/host unreachable) and should be dropped/replaced with the refs above. RouteAccuracy stays at 'medium' - the corridor and both endpoints are well-established by name, but without sourced coordinates this cannot support an upgrade to 'high'.

resolutions.start_name: Tarek gas field / junction (Khalda concession complex, Western Desert)
resolutions.end_name: Amreya (Ameriya), Alexandria Governorate

waypoints.name: Obaiyed gas field, Matruh Governorate (upstream origin of the wider Northern Gas Pipeline system)

resolutions.corridor_desc: Part of the 'Northern Gas Pipeline' / 'Western Desert Gas Project - North Line' corridor running from the Obaiyed gas field area (Matruh Governorate, northern Western Desert, Khalda/BAPETCO concession complex) roughly east-northeast across the Western Desert, picking up Khalda-concession gas near Tarek/Ras Kanayes, and terminating at the Amreya industrial/refinery area on the southwestern edge of Alexandria Governorate. I could not source precise coordinates for Obaiyed field or the Tarek junction from any independent, verifiable source (only qualitative geologic descriptions, e.g. 'largest Jurassic gas/condensate field in the northern Western Desert... western flank of the Matruh basin' from a SEG/AAPG abstract) — leaving those lat/lon null rather than inventing points. Amreya's coordinates are corroborated via Wikipedia (city, ~30.849N 29.612E) which is consistent with, though not identical to, the Amreya refinery's own published siting further north near the coast (~31.01N 29.84E per a third-party energy-infrastructure database) — both are within the same Amreya industrial cluster southwest of Alexandria. Given the length/capacity dispute above, treat this corridor suggestion as bounding the general Western-Desert-to-Amreya routing shared by the whole 3-segment system, not a precise fix for where the Obaiyed-Tarek/Tarek-Ameryia split point falls.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Only the Ameriya/Amreya endpoint could be sourced to a defensible coordinate; the Western Desert (Obaiyed/Tarek) end and the precise segment boundary point are not independently pinpointable from public sources found in this pass, so no coordinates are given for them (left null) rather than fabricated. Suggested accuracy is 'low' given both the coordinate gap and the unresolved length/capacity dispute over what exactly this segment covers.

resolutions.start_name: Salam gas plant (Khalda concession, Western Desert, Matruh Governorate)
resolutions.end_name: Marsa Matruh area (Matruh Terminal / city-supply receiving point on the Mediterranean coast)
resolutions.corridor_desc: Runs roughly NNE from the Salam gas processing plant in the Khalda concession (northern Western Desert) across the open desert of Matruh Governorate to the Mediterranean coast at/near Marsa Matruh. Straight-line separation is ~75 km, matching the GEM length; the actual routed path is unmapped, so the corridor is bounded by the two endpoints only. End point 'Matruh Terminal' is the coastal receiving/city-gate point serving Matruh Governorate.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from sources: OGJ/Offshore-Technology/oilandgasadvancement place the Salam gas plant on Apache's Khalda concession in the northern Western Desert and describe it supplying gas/LPG to Matruh Governorate; GulfPub gives the line as Salam field -> Matrouh. Marsa Matruh city coordinate (31.3525N, 27.2453E) is a well-known place. The Salam gas plant coordinate (30.7097N, 26.9769E = 30 42'35"N 26 58'37"E) is taken from a public map (Wikimapia) lead, NOT an authoritative source — flagged as approximate; it is corroborated only in that the resulting ~75 km straight-line matches the GEM/Egypt O&G length. No coordinates were fabricated; intermediate waypoints are unknown so none are given, and the corridor is left loosely bounded (suggested accuracy low).

resolutions.start_name: Abu Sennan / Badr El Din (BED-AS) field connector, Abu Gharadig Basin, northern Western Desert
resolutions.end_name: El Amreya (Ameryia) gas distribution / industrial area, west of Alexandria
resolutions.corridor_desc: Runs roughly north-northeast for ~160 km from the Abu Sennan/Badr El Din field complex in the Abu Gharadig Basin (northern Western Desert) across open desert to the Ameryia (El Amreya) coastal industrial/gas-distribution zone just west of Alexandria. Endpoints are named and independently placed (Abu Sennan field lat/lon from peer-reviewed literature; El Amreya is a named town/industrial zone on the coast); the interior alignment is NOT published, so treat the corridor as an approximate great-circle band between the two endpoints, loosely bounded.
resolutions.researcher_notes: End = Ameryia gas station, from petro-news (line 'heading to the Ameryia gas station') and the egyptoil PDF ('To: Ameryia'); El Amreya coordinates ~31.01N/29.80E are defensible from the named town west of Alexandria (approximate). Start = Abu Sennan/BED connector; coordinates ~29.58N/28.58E derived from the published Abu Sennan field extent 'between latitudes 29°30'N and 29°40'N and longitudes 28°30'E and 28°40'E' (PMC12332090). No coordinates were invented; interior waypoints left empty because no route geometry is published.

resolutions.pipeline_name: Badr El Din Spur Gas Pipelines
resolutions.start_name: Badr El Din (BED) fields, Western Desert (Matrouh Governorate)
resolutions.end_name: BED/Abu Sennan connector (junction feeding the BED/AS-Ameryia trunk), Abu Gharadig basin, northern Western Desert
resolutions.corridor_desc: Per the Egypt Oil & Gas Western Desert table the line runs from the Badr El Din (BED) producing fields to the 'BED/Abu Sennan connector', a gathering junction in the Abu Gharadig basin of the northern Western Desert where BED field gas ties into the BED/AS-Ameryia trunk (GEM P3936) toward Ameryia/Alexandria. Both endpoints are corroborated as real: the BED fields sit in Matrouh Governorate (BAPETCO acreage; Zawya/BAPETCO Badr-15 discovery), and the Abu Sennan concession is a 644 km2 block in the Abu Gharadig basin, northern Western Desert (NS Energy). The corridor therefore lies within the northern Western Desert / Abu Gharadig basin, roughly bounded 29.8-30.7 N, 27.5-28.7 E, trending generally eastward from the BED fields to the Abu Sennan connector. I could NOT source precise field/junction coordinates, so point lat/lon are left null rather than fabricated; the ~130 km stated length is itself single-sourced and disputed by GulfPub (which places comparable BED lines at 19-63 km), so even the corridor length is low-confidence. Bound is loose (basin-level).
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the source table (BED fields -> BED/Abu Sennan connector) and corroborated as real places by NS Energy (Abu Sennan concession, Abu Gharadig basin, northern Western Desert) and Zawya/BAPETCO (BED fields, Matrouh, Western Desert). No source gives a routed alignment or endpoint coordinates, so lat/lon left null and only a basin-level corridor bound is offered. Fabrication of coordinates avoided.

resolutions.pipeline_name: Badr El Din Spur Gas Pipelines
resolutions.start_name: Badr El Din / El Salam field cluster (Abu Gharadig basin, northern Western Desert)
resolutions.end_name: Abu Sennan field, Western Desert, Egypt
resolutions.corridor_desc: Existence is in doubt (see validity), so a route is premature. IF any line exists along this corridor, the OGJ CO2-EOR concept describes CO2-rich gas gathered from four Western Desert plants (Obaiyed, El Salam, Tarek, El Qasr) to a central point in the El Salam area, then a 130-mile line to the Abu Sennan field. All named places sit in the Abu Gharadig basin of the northern Western Desert, administratively spanning Matruh governorate, roughly between ~29.5-30.2 N and ~27.5-28.5 E. I do not have a defensible point geocode for the individual fields, so lat/lon are left null rather than fabricated; the bound is loose (basin-scale, ~1 degree box). Corridor runs generally west/northwest (El Salam/Obaiyed area) to east (Abu Sennan) across the Abu Gharadig oil/gas province.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints named from the OGJ CO2-EOR paper (El Salam gathering point -> Abu Sennan field) and GEM's own Start=Badr El Din Field. No point coordinates fabricated; only the basin-scale corridor is defensible from the named Abu Gharadig-basin fields. Route suggestion is contingent on the pipeline actually existing, which this audit disputes.

resolutions.start_name: Abu Gharadig gas processing plant (Abu Gharadig field, N Western Desert, Matruh governorate)
resolutions.end_name: Dahshour gas/LPG plant (Giza governorate, SW of Cairo)
resolutions.corridor_desc: Roughly W-E trunk across the northern Western Desert, ~262.5 km, from the Abu Gharadig gas plant eastward through mainly uninhabited desert to the Dahshour gas/LPG plant on the Nile-valley edge SW of Cairo. Endpoints are firmly sourced and named; the desert interior is unconstrained by waypoints, so the interior path is a loose bound (essentially a desert corridor, likely tracking near the parallel WDGP North Line / Cairo-Alexandria desert corridor). Start coordinate is APPROXIMATE — bounded to the Abu Gharadig field area (~29.6-29.9N, 28.0-28.5E per published basin/field studies); Dahshour endpoint is precisely known.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the Egypt Oil & Gas KPC feature (Abu Gharadig Plant -> Dahshour Plant, 'mainly uninhabited desert'). Dahshour coord = the well-known Dahshur/Dahshour site SW of Cairo (~29.79N, 31.22E). Abu Gharadig start coord approximated to the field area from published Abu Gharadig Basin location studies (BED-3/Sitra ~29.75-30.05N/27.5-28.2E; NEAG ~29.9N/29.9E, 127 km from Cairo) — NOT a fabricated point; no exact plant coordinate was sourceable so it is left approximate. No interior waypoints could be sourced.

resolutions.start_name: Zohr field wellhead/manifold platforms, Shorouk concession, offshore Mediterranean Sea (Egypt EEZ)
resolutions.end_name: El-Gamil onshore gas treatment plant, Port Said Governorate, Egypt
resolutions.corridor_desc: Two parallel ~216 km, 30-inch subsea pipelines run from the Zohr field's wellhead/manifold platforms in the Shorouk concession (Mediterranean Sea, ~1,450-1,500 m water depth, sourced by NS Energy/Eni as ~190 km north of Port Said) roughly due south across the Egyptian EEZ continental slope and shelf to landfall at El-Gamil on the Port Said coast, terminating at the El-Gamil onshore gas treatment plant (8 production trains + sulphur units). No public subsea route trace or intermediate waypoints were found, so the corridor here is a straight-line bound between two independently sourced named endpoints, not a traced path. Sanity check: the great-circle distance between the sourced field coordinate (Wikidata, rounded to 33.0N/32.5E) and the El-Gamil/Port Said-airport coordinate (OurAirports, 31.2793N/32.2406E) computes to ~193 km - closely matching the independently reported ~190 km distance, which corroborates the general bearing/scale even though the exact endpoint coordinates are approximate (field position is a rounded Wikidata value; the onshore end uses the nearest well-documented 'El-Gamil' point, the former RAF/Port Said airport, as a proxy for the plant, which is in the same immediate locale but not confirmed to be the exact plant site).
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named, independently-sourced places (Zohr/Shorouk field per Wikidata; El-Gamil per NS Energy + OurAirports' airport entry as the best-documented point in that exact locale). resolutions.corridor_desc: Per GASCO's ESIA/RAP for this project: a 42in line runs from a Rashid Petroleum Company facility east of Edko City, south along/near the Edko-Damanhour road, crossing the coastal road, the Alexandria-Rashid railway, Bousily Drain and Edko Drain, to a National Natural Gas Network facility north of Bisintaway village (~27 km). All of this is within Beheira Governorate, Nile Delta -- no need to reach the unrelated town of Dairut in Assiut/Upper Egypt; 'Dairut Power Station' as named in the ESIA is almost certainly a second, more local beneficiary tie-in along the same corridor, not the distant Assiut town, but I could not independently confirm which facility that name refers to and flag it for a human to check when drawing the actual route line. Start/end coordinates given are town-center approximations for Edko and Mahmoudiya (public gazetteer values), not the exact valve/plant siting, which the ESIA describes only in words and route-figure captions (no coordinates given in the source text).
